mainTopic: Group ברכות at a meal (reclining, wine, and who leads), and the ברכות over incense, spices, and scented oils.
overview: This amud opens at the end of the story of רב's students. A wise elder taught them that once a group decides to eat together at a set place, simply sitting counts like reclining. The גמרא then gives two opposite versions of רב's view on whether the משנה's reclining rule applies to wine. רבי יוחנן says wine works like bread. A ברייתא about the order of a formal meal challenges רב, and the גמרא defends both versions. בן זומא explains why each person blesses wine for himself during the meal but one blesses for all after it. The person who washes first at the end of the meal blesses the incense and leads ברכת המזון, and a story about רבי and רב shows this rule in action. The amud ends with ברכות over smells: when to bless incense, which ברכה fits which spice, the special ברכה for balsam oil, and a three-way argument about oils scented with spices.

steps.title: A student mourns רב again because no one knows the laws of ברכת המזון
steps.stepSummary: The student (רב אדא בר אהבה, from the previous page) turns his torn garment around and makes a new tear. He cries out that רב has died and they never learned the laws of ברכת המזון.
steps.simpleTranslation: He turned his torn garment so the tear was behind him, and made another tear. He said: רב has died, and we have not learned the laws of ברכת המזון!
steps.whatsHappening: This is the end of a story. A student of רב is mourning again because the group could not answer a basic question about ברכת המזון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the previous page, the students ate together after רב's funeral and could not decide whether one person could make the ברכה for everyone. The new tear shows the grief of losing their teacher's answers. It also sets up the question about sitting versus reclining.

keyTerms.meaning: Tearing a garment as a sign of mourning

phrases.english: He turned his tear around to his back,
phrases.notes: He moved the first mourning tear to the back of his garment.

phrases.english: and tore another tear.
phrases.notes: This is a fresh mourning tear.

phrases.english: He said: Rav has passed away,
and Birkat HaMazon we have not learned!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story from the previous page about רב's students after his funeral.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is an open question about one person making ברכת המזון for the group, and רב is no longer alive to answer it.

steps.title: An elder resolves the contradiction: setting a place to eat counts as reclining
steps.stepSummary: An elder points out a contradiction between the משנה and a ברייתא. He resolves it by explaining that when people say 'let's go eat bread at such-and-such place,' their sitting counts like reclining.
steps.simpleTranslation: Until a certain elder came. He pointed out a contradiction between the משנה and a ברייתא and resolved it: once they said, 'Let us go and eat bread at such-and-such a place,' it is as if they reclined.
steps.whatsHappening: An elder answers the students' question. He reconciles two sources that seemed to clash.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that people who merely sit to eat each make their own ברכה. A ברייתא says that people who sit down together, one makes the ברכה for all. The elder explains that the ברייתא is a case where the group planned to eat together at a set place. That shared plan makes their sitting as binding as formal reclining.

keyTerms.meaning: A tannaitic teaching outside the משנה
They reclined (the formal way of eating together)

steps.whatToRemember: A group that has decided to eat together at a set place counts as 'reclining,' even if they only sit. So one person can make the ברכה for all.
steps.whyThisMatters: The key factor is not body position but a shared, fixed meal. That idea explains when a group becomes one unit for ברכות.

phrases.english: Until a certain elder came,
he raised for them a contradiction between the Mishnah and the Baraita,
phrases.notes: משנה: sitting means each makes his own ברכה. ברייתא: sitting together means one makes the ברכה for all.

phrases.english: and he resolved it for them:

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן דְּאָמְרִי ״נֵיזִיל וְנֵיכוֹל לַחְמָא בְּדוּךְ פְּלָן״ —
phrases.english: since they said, 'Let us go and eat bread in such-and-such a place,'
it is considered as if they reclined.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַד דַּאֲתָא הָהוּא סָבָא, רְמָא לְהוּ מַתְנִיתִין אַבָּרַיְיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question that made the student mourn.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing cases: the ברייתא is a planned group meal, and the משנה is a casual one.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only literal reclining joins people together for one ברכה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Deciding together to eat at a set place makes sitting equal to reclining.

steps.title: רב: the משנה's reclining rule is only for bread, but wine does not need reclining
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה, 'if they reclined, one makes the ברכה.' רב says reclining is needed only for bread. For wine, reclining is not needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'If they reclined, one recites the blessing.' רב said: This was taught only about bread, which requires reclining. But wine does not require reclining.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה's rule and gives רב's limit on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, bread needs reclining before one person can make the ברכה for everyone. For wine, there is no such requirement, so even people who are just sitting can have one person make the ברכה for all. This makes wine easier than bread.

keyTerms.meaning: One person makes the ברכה for everyone

steps.confusionAlert: In this first version, 'wine does not need reclining' makes wine EASIER: one person can make the ברכה for all even without reclining. The second version (step 5) says the opposite.

phrases.english: 'If they reclined, one recites the blessing.'

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא פַּת
phrases.english: Rav said: They taught this only about bread,
which requires reclining,
but wine does not require reclining.
phrases.notes: Even when they only sit, one person can make the ברכה over wine for all.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא פַּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the story ends, the גמרא returns to analyzing the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Version 1 of רב: reclining is needed only for bread. For wine, one person can make the ברכה for all even without reclining.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: wine also requires reclining
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן disagrees with רב. Wine also requires reclining before one person can make the ברכה for everyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: Even wine also requires reclining.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives the opposing view to רב's first version.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוחנן, wine and bread follow the same rule. Without reclining, each person makes his own ברכה over wine.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
Even wine also requires reclining.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ יַיִן נָמֵי בָּעֵי הֲסִבָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב's first version.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wine, like bread, needs reclining before one person can make the ברכה for all.

steps.title: Second version of רב: reclining does not help for wine
steps.stepSummary: Some report רב differently. Reclining helps only for bread. For wine, reclining does not help, so each person always makes his own ברכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say רב said: This was taught only about bread, for which reclining is effective. But for wine, reclining is not effective.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second report of רב's opinion. It reverses the meaning for wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here wine is STRICTER than bread. Even if the group reclines, each person must make his own ברכה over wine. The point is no longer whether reclining is required, but whether it helps at all.
steps.confusionAlert: Both versions start with 'only bread,' but they lead to opposite results for wine. Version 1 makes wine easier (no reclining needed). Version 2 makes wine stricter (reclining does not help).

phrases.english: Some say: Rav said:
They taught this only about bread,
for which reclining is effective.
But wine,
reclining is not effective for it.
phrases.notes: Each person always makes his own ברכה over wine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different report of רב's view from step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Version 2 of רב: reclining joins people together only for bread. For wine, each person always makes his own ברכה.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן in the second version: reclining helps for wine too
steps.stepSummary: In this version, רבי יוחנן holds that reclining also works for wine, so one person can make the ברכה for all.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: Even for wine, reclining is effective.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן's opposing view, worded to match the second version of רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוחנן, wine and bread are treated the same. Once the group reclines, one person can make the ברכה over wine for everyone.
steps.whatToRemember: רב separates bread from wine (in one of two opposite ways). רבי יוחנן treats wine like bread in both versions.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ יַיִן נָמֵי מַהְנְיָא לֵיהּ הֲסִבָּה.
phrases.english: Even for wine, reclining is also effective.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ יַיִן נָמֵי מַהְנְיָא לֵיהּ הֲסִבָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב's second version.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Reclining lets one person make the ברכה over wine for everyone.

steps.title: A ברייתא on the order of a formal meal challenges רב
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא describes a formal meal. Before reclining, each guest blesses the wine himself. After they recline, one person blesses the wine for everyone. This seems to go against רב in both versions.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: What is the order of reclining? Guests come in and sit on benches and chairs until everyone has arrived. Water is brought and each washes one hand. Wine is brought and each blesses for himself. Then they go up and recline, and water is brought. Even though each already washed one hand, he washes both hands again. Wine is brought, and even though each already blessed for himself, one blesses for all.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to challenge רב. The answer will come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before reclining, each guest blesses the wine separately. This means wine does need reclining, against רב's first version. After reclining, one person blesses the wine for all. This means reclining does help for wine, against רב's second version. Both readings support רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: The order of a formal reclining meal

steps.confusionAlert: There are two rounds of wine and two washings. The first round happens while sitting, before the meal, so each person blesses himself. The second round happens after reclining, so one person blesses for all. The challenge comes from comparing the two rounds.

phrases.english: They objected: What is the order of reclining?
Guests enter and sit

phrases.aramaic: עַל גַּבֵּי סַפְסָלִין וְעַל גַּבֵּי קָתֶדְרָאוֹת
phrases.english: on benches and on chairs
until all of them have entered.
Water was brought to them:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד נוֹטֵל יָדוֹ אַחַת.
phrases.english: each one washes one hand.
phrases.notes: Just one hand, enough to hold the cup.

phrases.english: Wine came to them:
each one blesses for himself.
phrases.notes: This is while they're sitting, not yet reclining.

phrases.english: They went up and reclined, and water came to them,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁכָּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד נָטַל יָדוֹ אַחַת,
phrases.english: even though each one already washed one hand,
he washes both hands again.
Wine came to them:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁכָּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד בֵּרַךְ לְעַצְמוֹ,
phrases.english: even though each one already blessed for himself,
one blesses for all of them.
phrases.notes: After reclining, one ברכה over wine covers the whole group.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges both versions of רב's view.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Before reclining, each person blesses the wine himself, so wine needs reclining (against version 1). After reclining, one blesses the wine for all, so reclining helps for wine (against version 2).

steps.title: The first part of the ברייתא challenges the first version of רב
steps.stepSummary: According to the version where wine does not need reclining, the רישא of the ברייתא, where each guest blesses the wine for himself before reclining, is difficult.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the version where רב said: 'This was only taught about bread, which needs reclining, but wine does not need reclining,' the first part of the ברייתא is difficult!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא focuses its challenge on the first version of רב, using the first part of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, wine does not need reclining, so people simply sitting together should already count as a group, and one person could bless for everyone. But the רישא says that before reclining, each guest blesses the wine himself. That suggests sitting is not enough for wine, which goes against רב.

keyTerms.meaning: Version, or way of reporting a statement
'They only taught this about...', which limits a teaching
The first part of a teaching

steps.confusionAlert: In this version, 'wine does not need reclining' is a lenient view. It means one person can bless for all even without reclining. It does not mean that reclining never matters for wine.

phrases.english: According to that version in which Rav said

phrases.aramaic: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא פַּת דְּבָעֵי הֲסִבָּה,
phrases.english: they only taught this about bread, which requires reclining,
but wine does not require reclining —
phrases.notes: In this version, sitting together is enough for wine.

phrases.english: the first clause is difficult!
phrases.notes: The first clause says that before reclining, each guest blesses for himself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the general challenge from step 7 to the first version of רב and the רישא of the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב, first version (step 3): wine does not need reclining
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If sitting is enough for wine, the guests sitting before reclining should already be a group. Yet the ברייתא has each one bless for himself.

steps.title: Guests in the waiting room plan to move on
steps.stepSummary: Guests are different: while they wait before the meal, they intend to get up and move to the dining room, so they are not yet a group.
steps.simpleTranslation: Guests are different, because they intend to get up and leave that place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge to the first version of רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sitting together counts as a group for wine only when people plan to stay. The guests in the front room know they will soon get up and go into the dining room, so their sitting there does not join them together. That is why each one blesses for himself, and רב's rule still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different, a case set apart
Their intention is to get up and move away

phrases.english: Guests are different,
for their intention is to get up and leave.
phrases.notes: They plan to move from the waiting area to the dining room.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: the case in the ברייתא is a special situation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Guests sitting before the meal are like any people sitting together, so one should bless for all.
steps.terutzMaskana: Their plan to leave keeps them from being a group, so the ברייתא fits the first version of רב.

steps.title: The last part of the ברייתא challenges the second version of רב
steps.stepSummary: According to the version where reclining does not help for wine, the סיפא of the ברייתא, where one person blesses the wine for all after reclining, is difficult.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to the version where רב said: 'They only taught that reclining helps for bread, but for wine reclining does not help,' the last part of the ברייתא is difficult!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns to the second version of רב and challenges it from the last part of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the second version, reclining never lets one person bless the wine for others. But the סיפא says that once they have reclined, one person blesses the wine for everyone. That openly contradicts this version.

keyTerms.meaning: The last part of a teaching

phrases.english: And according to that version in which Rav said

phrases.aramaic: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא פַּת, דְּמַהְנְיָא לֵיהּ הֲסִבָּה,
phrases.english: they only taught this about bread, for which reclining is effective,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל יַיִן לָא מַהְנְיָא לֵיהּ הֲסִבָּה —
phrases.english: but for wine reclining is not effective —
phrases.notes: Each person must always bless the wine himself.

phrases.english: the last clause is difficult!
phrases.notes: The last clause says that after reclining, one person blesses the wine for all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the first version, now defended, to the second version of רב.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב, second version (step 5): reclining does not help for wine
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא has one person bless the wine for all after reclining, which shows that reclining does help for wine.

steps.title: Reclining for bread carries over to the wine
steps.stepSummary: The case in the ברייתא is different: since the reclining works for the bread, it also works for the wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: There it is different: since reclining works for the bread, it also works for the wine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge to the second version of רב, and this closes the defense of רב in both versions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב meant that reclining does not help for wine drunk on its own. In the ברייתא, the guests recline for a bread meal, and that reclining joins them for the bread. Because of that (a מגו), it joins them for the wine at that meal too.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Since...': because one thing applies, a related thing applies too

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא fits רב in both versions. In version 1, guests waiting before the meal are not a group because they plan to move. In version 2, reclining that works for bread carries over to the wine at that meal.
steps.whyThisMatters: The answer shows that wine at a bread meal is treated together with the meal, unlike wine drunk on its own.

phrases.english: There it is different,

phrases.aramaic: דְּמִגּוֹ דְּקָא מַהְנְיָא לֵיהּ הֲסִבָּה לְפַת —
phrases.english: for since reclining is effective for the bread —
reclining is effective for the wine too.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאנֵי הָתָם דְּמִגּוֹ דְּקָא מַהְנְיָא לֵיהּ הֲסִבָּה לְפַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: a מגו extension from bread to wine
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The סיפא shows that reclining helps for wine in general.
steps.terutzMaskana: Reclining helps for wine only because it already works for the bread meal. Wine drunk on its own still needs a ברכה from each person.

steps.title: Why does each person bless wine for himself during the meal?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about wine served during the meal. It then brings a question that was asked to בן זומא: why does each person bless for himself during the meal, while after the meal one person blesses for everyone?
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: If wine was brought to them during the meal, each person blesses for himself. They asked בן זומא: Why did the חכמים say that if wine comes during the meal, each person blesses for himself, but if it comes after the meal, one person blesses for everyone?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new line of the משנה and asks for the reason behind it. This step sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a group that is eating together can have one person bless for everyone. So it is surprising that during the meal each person blesses the wine alone, while after the meal one person can bless for all. The question asks what makes these two times different.

phrases.english: The משנה says: Wine came to them during the meal.
They asked Ben Zoma:
Why did they say
if wine came to them during the meal,
each and every one blesses for himself,
but if it came after the meal,
one blesses for all of them?

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאֲלוּ אֶת בֶּן זוֹמָא: מִפְּנֵי מָה אָמְרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the discussion of reclining to the next line of the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason why wine served during the meal needs a separate ברכה from each person, while wine served after the meal gets one ברכה for everyone

steps.title: בן זומא: the throat is busy during the meal
steps.stepSummary: בן זומא answers that during the meal people's throats are busy with food, so they cannot all drink together at the same moment.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: Because the throat is not free.
steps.whatsHappening: בן זומא gives the reason for the משנה's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While people are eating, each person is in the middle of chewing and swallowing, and no one is ready to drink at the same time as the others. If one person blessed for everyone, they would all have to stop and wait for each other. So during the meal each person blesses whenever he is ready. After the meal everyone is free, so one person can bless for all.

keyTerms.meaning: The throat (literally: the place of swallowing)

steps.whatToRemember: During the meal each person blesses the wine himself because people are busy eating and cannot drink together. After the meal one person blesses for all.

phrases.english: He said to them:
Since the throat is not free.
phrases.notes: While eating, people are not all ready to drink at the same time

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question asked to בן זומא
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: During the meal people's throats are busy with food, so they cannot drink at one shared moment, and each person blesses for himself.

steps.title: Why does the wine-blesser also bless the incense?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says that the one who blessed the wine after the meal also blesses the מוגמר. The extra words 'and he' suggest there is someone else more fitting, so the גמרא asks why this person gets the honor.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: And he says the ברכה over the incense. Since the משנה says 'and he says the ברכה over the incense,' this implies there is someone better suited than him. So why does he say it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the משנה's wording closely and raises a challenge. It asks why this particular person blesses the incense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה could have just said that a ברכה is said over the incense. Instead it says 'and he,' meaning that same person who blessed the wine. That stress suggests someone else might have had a stronger claim, so the גמרא wants to know what gives this person the right.

keyTerms.meaning: Incense, spices burned on coals after a meal
From the fact that it teaches
Better than him, more fitting than him

phrases.english: The משנה says: And he says the blessing over the incense, etc.
From the fact that it teaches 'and he says over the incense,'
it implies that there is someone better suited than him,
so why does he say it?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִדְּקָתָנֵי ״וְהוּא אוֹמֵר עַל הַמּוּגְמָר״, מִכְלָל דְּאִיכָּא עֲדִיף מִינֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next line of the משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's words 'and he says over the incense'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The stress on 'he' suggests someone else is more fitting, so it is unclear why the one who blessed the wine gets this honor

steps.title: He washed his hands first at the end of the meal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that he blesses the incense because he was the first to wash his hands at the end of the meal.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because he washed his hands first at the end of the meal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why this person gets the honor of blessing the incense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Washing hands at the end of the meal (מים אחרונים) and the incense both serve to freshen people up after eating. Whoever went first in the washing is treated as the leading person for the end of the meal. So he also gets to bless the incense.

keyTerms.meaning: At the end, meaning the washing after the meal (מַיִם אַחֲרוֹנִים)

phrases.english: Since he washed his hands
first at the final washing.
phrases.notes: מים אחרונים, the washing after the meal

steps.triggerLanguage: הוֹאִיל וְהוּא נָטַל יָדָיו תְּחִלָּה בָּאַחֲרוֹנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of why he blesses the incense
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies a reason for giving this person the honor
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Someone else should have blessed the incense
steps.terutzMaskana: The person who washed first at the end of the meal is the leader of the end of the meal, so he blesses the incense

steps.title: This supports רב: the first to wash leads ברכת המזון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that this fits רב's rule that whoever washes first at the end of the meal is the one chosen to lead ברכת המזון.
steps.simpleTranslation: This supports רב, as רב חייא בר אשי said in the name of רב: Whoever washes his hands first at the end of the meal is the one chosen to lead the ברכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the answer it just gave matches an existing ruling of רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב taught that washing first at the end of the meal marks a person as the leader of ברכת המזון. The answer about the incense uses the same idea: going first in one end-of-meal מצוה gives you priority in the others. So the משנה, as explained, supports רב.

keyTerms.meaning: Designated, ready, to lead the ברכה (ברכת המזון)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the practice that the person who washes מים אחרונים first is the one who leads ברכת המזון.

phrases.english: This supports Rav,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: as Rav Ḥiyya bar Ashi said that Rav said:
One who washes his hands first at the final washing
is designated for the blessing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the answer in step 15 matches רב's ruling
steps.raayaObject: רב's rule that the one who washes first at the end of the meal leads ברכת המזון
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה, as explained in step 15, which gives the incense ברכה to the one who washed first

steps.title: Story: רבי tells רב to wash his hands
steps.stepSummary: At a meal, רבי told רב to get up and wash his hands. רב was afraid he was being criticized, and רבי חייא explained that רבי meant he should get ready to lead ברכת המזון.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב and רבי חייא were sitting before רבי at a meal. רבי said to רב: Get up and wash your hands. רבי חייא saw that רב was trembling. רבי חייא said to him: Son of nobles, he is telling you to look over ברכת המזון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that shows רב's rule in action.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב thought that being told to wash meant he had done something wrong, like having dirty hands or eating too much. רבי חייא explained that washing first means being chosen to lead ברכת המזון, so רבי was giving him an honor. This shows how real and well known the rule was.

keyTerms.meaning: Get up and wash your hand
Son of nobles, a term of respect

steps.whatToRemember: Whoever washes first at the end of the meal is the one who leads ברכת המזון, and he also blesses the incense.

phrases.english: Rav and Rabbi Ḥiyya were sitting
before Rabbi at a meal.
Rabbi said to Rav:
Get up, wash your hand.
He (Rabbi Ḥiyya) saw that he (Rav) was trembling.
Rabbi Ḥiyya said to him:
Son of nobles,
he is telling you: look over Grace after Meals.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב וְרַבִּי חִיָּיא הֲווֹ יָתְבִי קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי בִּסְעוֹדְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A story that shows רב's rule from step 16 being applied
steps.raayaObject: The rule that the first to wash at the end of the meal leads ברכת המזון
steps.raayaSupportSource: A story at רבי's meal, where telling רב to wash meant he would lead ברכת המזון

steps.title: When to bless over the smell of incense
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא quotes רבא בר ירמיה: the ברכה over incense smell is said once the column of smoke rises.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said in the name of רבא בר ירמיה: From when do we say the ברכה over a smell? From the time its column of smoke goes up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic, ברכות over smells, which grows out of the מוגמר in the משנה. It gives a rule for the right moment to say the ברכה over incense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Incense is put on hot coals, and the smoke rises in a column. According to רבא בר ירמיה, that rising smoke is the signal to say the ברכה. He does not require waiting until the person actually smells it.

keyTerms.meaning: Its column (of smoke), rising like a palm tree

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא אָמַר רָבָא בַּר יִרְמְיָה:
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said that Rava bar Yirmeya said:
From when does one bless over the scent?
From when its column of smoke rises.
phrases.notes: תמרה is a column shaped like a palm tree.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from who blesses the מוגמר to when the ברכה over its smell is said.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ברכה over incense is said once the smoke column rises, before actually smelling it.

steps.title: But he has not smelled it yet
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא objects: at the moment the smoke rises, the person has not yet smelled anything.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said to רבא בר ירמיה: But he has not smelled it yet!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא challenges the rule. How can you bless over a smell you have not experienced yet?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The assumption behind the challenge is that a ברכה over pleasure should come when the pleasure is actually there. When the smoke first rises, the smell has not reached the person yet, so the ברכה seems too early.

keyTerms.meaning: But look, but surely (introduces a challenge)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי זֵירָא לְרָבָא בַּר יִרְמְיָה:
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said to Rava bar Yirmeya:
But he has not smelled it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the timing set in step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא בר ירמיה's rule to bless when the smoke rises
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברכה over a smell should only be said once there is actually a smell to enjoy.

steps.title: Like המוציא before eating, what counts is the intention
steps.stepSummary: רבא בר ירמיה answers that המוציא is also said before eating. What matters is that the person intends to eat, and here the person intends to smell.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: By your logic, when someone says המוציא, he hasn't eaten yet either! Rather, it's enough that he plans to eat. Here too, it's enough that he plans to smell.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא בר ירמיה answers by comparing the case to the ברכה on bread. Everyone agrees that ברכה is said before eating.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blessings over enjoyment are said before the enjoyment, as long as the person is ready and intends to enjoy it. Once the smoke rises, the smell is ready and the person is about to smell it, so the ברכה fits then.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to your reasoning (turns the questioner's logic back on him)
The ברכה on bread: 'Who brings forth bread from the earth'

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the ברכה is said after smelling. Like all ברכות on enjoyment, it comes right before, once the person is ready to enjoy.

phrases.english: He said to him: And according to your reasoning,
'Who brings forth bread from the earth' that one blesses,
but he has not eaten yet!
Rather, his intention is to eat;
here too, his intention is to smell.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends step 18 against the challenge in step 19.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A ברכה over pleasure can only be said once the pleasure is actually experienced.
steps.terutzMaskana: A ברכה is said when the person is ready and intends to enjoy, just like המוציא before eating.
steps.whatToRemember: ברכות over enjoyment are said before the enjoyment, once the person is ready and intends to enjoy. For incense, that moment is when the smoke rises.

steps.title: All incense gets בורא עצי בשמים except musk
steps.stepSummary: Through a chain of rabbis (רב, or some say זעירי), the rule is that all incense gets בורא עצי בשמים, except musk, which comes from an animal and gets בורא מיני בשמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא son of אבא בר נחמני said in the name of רב חסדא in the name of רב, and some say רב חסדא said it in the name of זעירי: Over all incense we say בורא עצי בשמים, except musk. Since it comes from an animal, we say בורא מיני בשמים over it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new rule about which ברכה to say over different kinds of incense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Most incense comes from plants and trees, so the ברכה mentions 'trees.' Musk comes from an animal, so 'trees' does not fit, and it gets the general ברכה of 'kinds of spices.' The two versions of the attribution only disagree about who said the rule, not about what it says.

keyTerms.meaning: Kinds of incense burned on coals
'Who creates fragrant trees', the ברכה over fragrant wood or plants
Musk, a perfume taken from an animal
'Who creates various spices', the general ברכה over fragrances

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בְּרֵיהּ דְּאַבָּא בַּר נַחְמָנִי
phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya son of Abba bar Nachmani said
that Rav Chisda said that Rav said,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר זְעֵירִי:
phrases.english: and some say Rav Chisda said that Ze'iri said:
Over all incense one blesses
'Who creates fragrant trees,'
except for musk, which comes from an animal,
over which one blesses 'Who creates various spices.'

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל הַמּוּגְמָרוֹת מְבָרְכִין עֲלֵיהֶן בּוֹרֵא עֲצֵי בְּשָׂמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from when to bless over incense to which ברכה to say.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All incense gets בורא עצי בשמים, except musk, which gets בורא מיני בשמים.

steps.title: A ברייתא challenges the blessing on burned incense
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says בורא עצי בשמים is only said over balsam from the house of רבי, balsam from the house of the Caesar, and myrtle anywhere. That contradicts 'all incense.'
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged this from a ברייתא: We only say בורא עצי בשמים over balsam from the house of רבי, balsam from the house of the Caesar, and myrtle wherever it grows!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the rule from step 21 with an earlier source, a ברייתא, which seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 21 gave בורא עצי בשמים even to burned incense. The ברייתא names balsam and myrtle, plants whose wood is itself there and gives off the smell. Rashi explains that this is not a closed list: the same holds for anything similar whose wood smells by itself without burning, and myrtle is named because it is common. What the ברייתא leaves out is burned incense, where the wood is gone and only the smoke rises. That is what contradicts the rule in step 21.

phrases.english: They raised an objection: One does not bless 'Who creates fragrant trees'

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא עַל אֲפַרְסְמוֹן שֶׁל בֵּית רַבִּי,
phrases.english: except over balsam of the house of Rabbi,
and over balsam of the house of Caesar,
and over myrtle everywhere!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rule in step 21 using a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that all incense gets בורא עצי בשמים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא gives that ברכה to fragrant wood that is itself present (balsam, myrtle, and per Rashi anything similar), not to burned incense, so it cannot apply to all incense.

steps.title: The rule is refuted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the challenge cannot be answered. The statement from step 21 is refuted.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא admits that the ברייתא wins. The rule that all incense gets בורא עצי בשמים is rejected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אמורא cannot argue with a ברייתא, and the גמרא finds no way to reconcile them. So the rule from רב or זעירי is overturned: burned incense does not get בורא עצי בשמים. Per Rashi, fragrant wood that smells by itself, like the balsam and myrtle the ברייתא names and anything similar, still does; over burned incense one says בורא מיני בשמים. Tosafot reports a different reading from the בה״ג, whose text has no תיובתא here and reads the ברייתא as myrtle and anything like it, meaning things grown mainly for their smell.

keyTerms.meaning: A conclusive refutation; the statement is rejected

steps.whatToRemember: The rule that all incense gets בורא עצי בשמים was refuted by a ברייתא. That ברכה is for fragrant wood that smells by itself (balsam, myrtle and, per Rashi, anything similar), not for burned incense.

phrases.english: It is a refutation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the challenge in step 22 by accepting it.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The statement in step 21 is refuted. בורא עצי בשמים is not said over all incense.

steps.title: רב חסדא asks about the blessing on balsam oil
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא asks רב יצחק which ברכה is said over balsam oil.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said to רב יצחק: This balsam oil, what blessing do we say over it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question. רב חסדא wants to know the ברכה for the smell of balsam oil.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We just learned that 'בורא עצי בשמים' is said over balsam itself. Balsam oil is a special and precious item, so רב חסדא asks whether it gets its own unique ברכה.

keyTerms.meaning: Balsam, a very precious fragrant plant

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב חִסְדָּא לְרַב יִצְחָק:
phrases.english: Rav Chisda said to Rav Yitzchak:
This balsam oil,
what blessing do we say over it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question about balsam oil, after the ברייתא in step 22 discussed balsam itself.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The correct ברכה for the smell of balsam oil.

steps.title: רב יהודה's blessing: Who creates the oil of our land
steps.stepSummary: רב יצחק quotes רב יהודה: the ברכה is 'בורא שמן ארצנו.'
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: This is what רב יהודה said: 'Who creates the oil of our land.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב יצחק answers by quoting רב יהודה. The ברכה mentions 'our land,' meaning ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Balsam grew only in ארץ ישראל. So רב יהודה made the ברכה praise ה' for the special oil of our land.

keyTerms.meaning: Who creates the oil of our land

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לֵיהּ, הָכִי אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה:
phrases.english: He said to him: This is what Rav Yehuda said:
'Who creates the oil of our land.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לֵיהּ, הָכִי אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: According to רב יהודה, the ברכה is 'בורא שמן ארצנו.'

steps.title: What does everyone else say?
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says רב יהודה's wording came from his great love of ארץ ישראל, and asks what the ברכה is for everyone else.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Except for רב יהודה, who loved ארץ ישראל very much, what does everyone else say?
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא does not accept רב יהודה's wording as the general rule. He asks again what most people should say.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא sees 'ארצנו' as a personal wording that shows רב יהודה's love for ארץ ישראל. He is not attacking the answer. He wants the standard ברכה that applies to everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: Except for him; leaving him aside

steps.confusionAlert: רב חסדא is not saying רב יהודה is wrong. He is saying רב יהודה's wording was personal, and he wants the general ברכה.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לֵיהּ: בַּר מִינֵּיהּ דְּרַב יְהוּדָה
phrases.english: He said to him: Except for Rav Yehuda,
to whom Eretz Yisrael was beloved,
what does everyone else say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the answer of step 25 to רב יהודה personally and asks again for the general rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The standard ברכה over balsam oil for ordinary people.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's blessing: Who creates pleasant oil
steps.stepSummary: רב יצחק quotes רבי יוחנן: everyone says 'בורא שמן ערב.'
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: This is what רבי יוחנן said: 'Who creates pleasant oil.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב יצחק gives the general answer from רבי יוחנן. The ברכה over balsam oil is 'בורא שמן ערב.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: This wording praises the oil's pleasant smell without mentioning ארץ ישראל. Because balsam oil is so special, it gets its own ברכה instead of the general 'בורא עצי בשמים.'
steps.whatToRemember: Balsam oil gets its own special ברכה: 'בורא שמן ערב' (רבי יוחנן). רב יהודה's 'שמן ארצנו' was his personal wording from love of ארץ ישראל.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לֵיהּ: הָכִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: He said to him: This is what Rabbi Yochanan said:
'Who creates pleasant oil.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the follow-up question of step 26.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: For everyone, the ברכה over balsam oil is 'בורא שמן ערב.'

steps.title: רב אדא בר אהבה: the spice itself, but not pressed oil
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה says 'בורא עצי בשמים' is said over costus, but not over oil pressed with spices.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה said: Over costus we say 'Who creates fragrant trees,' but over pressed oil, no.
steps.whatsHappening: A new ruling begins. רב אדא בר אהבה says the spice gets 'בורא עצי בשמים,' but oil that only took on its scent does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In pressed oil, the spices were pressed together with the oil so the oil soaked up their smell. רב אדא בר אהבה holds that only the spice itself gets this ברכה. Oil that only borrowed the smell does not. This is the strictest view in the argument that follows.

keyTerms.meaning: Pressed oil: oil pressed with spices so it absorbs their scent

phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava said:
Over this costus we say the blessing
'Who creates fragrant trees,'
but over pressed oil, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: which spice-scented oils get 'בורא עצי בשמים.'
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The spice itself gets 'בורא עצי בשמים,' but oil pressed with spices does not.

steps.title: רב כהנא: even pressed oil, but not ground oil
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא says even pressed oil gets 'בורא עצי בשמים,' but oil with spices ground into it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב כהנא said: Even pressed oil, but ground oil, no.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא disagrees with רב אדא בר אהבה and is more lenient. He includes pressed oil, but stops at ground oil.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pressed oil soaks up a strong scent from the spices. Ground oil, where spices were ground and mixed in, is a weaker preparation. רב כהנא draws his line between these two kinds.

keyTerms.meaning: Ground oil: oil into which spices were ground

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב כָּהֲנָא אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ מִשְׁחָא כְּבִישָׁא,
phrases.english: And Rav Kahana said: Even pressed oil,
but ground oil, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב כָּהֲנָא אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ מִשְׁחָא כְּבִישָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Argues with step 28 and widens the ruling to include pressed oil.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Pressed oil also gets 'בורא עצי בשמים,' but ground oil does not.

steps.title: The נהרדעי: even ground oil
steps.stepSummary: The נהרדעי say that even ground oil gets 'בורא עצי בשמים.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The נהרדעי say: Even ground oil.
steps.whatsHappening: The third and most lenient opinion is given. The נהרדעי say even ground oil gets 'בורא עצי בשמים.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: This finishes a three-step ladder of opinions. רב אדא בר אהבה allows only the spice itself, רב כהנא adds pressed oil, and the נהרדעי add even ground oil. For the נהרדעי, any oil that carries the spice's smell gets the ברכה.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages of Nehardea, a major Torah center in Bavel

steps.whatToRemember: There are three levels for spice-scented oil. רב אדא בר אהבה: only the spice itself. רב כהנא: also pressed oil. נהרדעי: even ground oil.

phrases.english: The Sages of Nehardea say: Even ground oil.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes one step further than רב כהנא in step 29 and includes ground oil.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even ground oil gets 'בורא עצי בשמים.'
